verdict.rationale: Homebrew's first-party docs describe committing a Brewfile to a project repository and having users run a single `brew bundle` command to install all declared project dependencies and start services. This works across formulae, casks, taps and other package types, and in CI such as GitHub Actions. missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration that `brew bundle install` reliably bootstraps a fresh clone, and evidence of version pinning or locking so installs are reproducible across machines.

support.subject: As a developer, I can bootstrap a fresh clone with one command that installs everything the project declares

citations.quote: It allows you to tell users to run a single command to install all dependencies for a project and start any services.
Adding a `Brewfile` to a project's repository (like you might a `package.json`, `Gemfile` or `requirements.txt`) is a nicer way of encoding project dependencies for developer environments.
one command can set up project dependencies across these environments and in continuous-integration services such as GitHub Actions.
You can use this behaviour in scripts like so: brew bundle check || brew bundle install
